title: Qantas hitting new lows?
body:
O.P.
His a direct comparison I had to call up Virgin Airlines to change my flight due to covid and I had a flight with Qantas I also needed changing.
Virigin - Wait time 4/5 (1min) -Friendliness 5/5 -Helpfulness 5/5 Overall 5/5 Got my money back and could've just as easily changed my flight to a later date at no cost
Qantas - Wait time 1/5 (approx 15min each time) x3 -Friendliness 1/5 -Helpfulness 1/5 Overall -5
Why was Qantas so bad? They didn't know their policies and they were so incredibly rude. After explaining to the arrogant woman that it was a Covid related change and she shouldn't be charging me over $150 in change fees (not even fair difference). I asked to speak to a local team member or her manager (yes I pulled a K...) needless to say the woman laughed. Said no. She will not transfer me as she has no reason to. I was dumb founded I couldn't believe it.
No matter how much I tried to explain it to her she kept saying these are the fees you called the booking line. I explained it's the only damn number I can call to resolve this issue with their policy!
Yes I know how bad it's been as of late – but this just takes the cake. Is this there new approach of customer service to rote customers?

[User #55240613877 postscreampuffWhirlpool Forums Addict] Did you meet the conditions on the QF website for free Covid changes?

If, in the week before you fly, you or anyone in your booking receive a positive COVID-19 test result, you can change your travel dates without incurring a change fee. Simply  contact your local Qantas office or your travel agent to change your booking. A fare difference may apply."

When this happens you have a number of options:
1. say you need to go to go, and call the call centre back and hope to get another operator;
2. let the transaction go through and complain to Customer Care. You can also complain about the operator who "helped" you to Customer Care if you can remember their name; and
3. as last resort dispute the charge with your credit card company against the ticket rules.
creampuff writes...
I was surprised by your post as you said you got through in 15 minutes, rather than 15 hours.
Qantas wait times are actually much more reasonable now.
They have done this by putting on lots of new staff in their Suva and Cape Town call centres.
The big challenge for Qantas is now quality control, especially as call centre staff are new, inexperienced, still learning Qantas policies, etc and frequently hang up on customers or end calls prematurely and promise to "call back" to move the calls along.

[User #77376564 postsBob9ludditeParticipant] Qantas are now dead to me – I will never use them again unless I absolutely have to. That might not seem a lot to some people, but I have been flying with Qantas since 1980s – domestic and international – both a Frequent Flyer and Qantas Club member – for a massive number of flights (over 1000). Last time we flew Qantas overseas (2018) it was a bit of an issue – and the problems we had were never answered. Since then we flew Singapore Airlines and Thai Airways. Due to Covid, I had a heap of Qantas points saved up from credit card purchases since 2018 so I used them all up for our first overseas flights. I sincerely regret that and will never make that mistake again. The problem is customer service – not the pilots, planes or schedules. I had an airport logistics issue that needed addressing (yes it is serious) and the local airport has been very helpful, but to get it compeltely sorted I had to talk to Qantas. All weekend I tried – web and phone – no one was able to help – because it was the weekend was main excuse. IMO their whole customer service 'front end interface' is about getting callers to use the website (and piss off). I tried again this morning (Monday) and after waiting nearly 15 minutes on the QC/FF number, I was given a recorded message from a non-english speaking person (probably overseas call centre) – "we are upgrading our system, please call back after few hours" – they then terminated my call. So I rang the specific 'Qantas Customer Care' number and after being on hold for 21 minutes I explained my problem. I was told that I had to call 'Qantas Agency Direct'. I tried the number they gave me and it didn't work, so I found the number online, and they will only speak to registered IATA members (Booking Agents). So I rang back the Qantas Customer Care number again and after being on hold for 27 minutes I advised the problem, and after waiting another 10 minutes the operator solved the problem for me (I hope). When the call ended I was asked to rate the call – the ratings I gave were about the operator and I gave the highest rating. But I bet the general manager of 'customer service' uses those ratings to say their service is good for his/her bonuses – but it is total crap – I was just lucky to get a good operator. Qantas = best pilots, best planes, best maintenance – WORST customer service. The majority of people want customer service first – there are so few airline disasters these days – extremely rare for any of the big carriers. No more Qantas.

[User #4811711481 postsNo. 48117Whirlpool Forums Addict] Last time I flew Qantas was in 2018, from Melbourne to Singapore return.
Couldn't complain about the service, it was good and food was okay too. Got the regular comfort pack / pillows etc and overall it was a comfortable flight experience. Flew both ways on A330s and I liked the 2-4-2 layout as opposed to 3-3-3 etc.
I haven't flew them since, but my main interest is building up QFF points and then redeeming classic reward business class flights with its partners.
For domestic, I'd generally check Jetstar first and if the price differential is not much between JQ and QF, I'd of course pick QF.
It did happen the once in that a Qantas flight from Melbourne to Sydney was cheaper than Jetstar, so on that occasion I booked Qantas.
I just hope that if the next time I book via Qantas, I won't have a horror story which seems these days, ubiquitous.
[User #809372277 postsSDHSortino RatioForum Regular] Let me add to this with a business practice I stumbled upon last week – ghost flights that appear in the Qantas schedule, but don’t seem to materialise in practice.
Booked a Hob-Per flight early last week for March NEXT YEAR. A couple of days later I got one of those “your flight has changed” emails. The direct flight I booked was pulled and I’d have to stopover somewhere. So I did a little digging on social media and it seems it’s a frequent Qantas practice. They keep the direct flight in the schedule and then once booked, say “oops, change of plans.”
I phoned them up and although there was no hesitation in agreeing to a refund, that promised refund will take 6-8 weeks!! Like, seriously, they could process it immediately if they wanted to.
The upside? Booked Virgin and it ended up being $100 cheaper.
Joyce is a fraudster whose sole objective is to enhance his personal net worth. Shame on Richard Goyder for enabling him.

Don't know about his own net worth but qantas is trying every possible way to hoodwink customers!
Not sure if any of you got one of those "Thank you from Qantas" with an apology and $50 off voucher email. Almost impossible for me to meet all the conditions attached to their generous $50 BS offer. Basically they are forcing you to make a payment to book in order to use the voucher and it has to be a return flight, and you are not allowed to use points (or points +pay) which I have plenty accumulated in the last two years. Look at these conditions for a bloody $50. Absolute joke!
- Promo code has to be accepted by 30 September 2022. Your promo code can be used to make a single itinerary Qantas operated return booking on qantas.com by 30 November 2022 for travel by 30 June 2023. - All domestic or international return bookings must depart from Australia. - A booking must contain only Qantas operated flights with a QF flight number to be eligible for the $50 discount. - The flight promo code cannot be redeemed in conjunction with Qantas Flight Credits, Points Plus Play, Classic Flight Rewards and cannot be added or applied after the ticket has been purchased. - The following payment forms can be used when using your unique flight promo code: credit/debit card, BPAY, POLi, PayPal or Zip. - The flight promo code is single use only. Once the code has been redeemed against a flight booking, it is no longer valid and cannot be used again. - Only one flight promo code can be used per booking. - An eligible booking must contain one individual adult only, bookings for multiple passengers are not eligible. Separate bookings must be made for any additional passengers.
[User #1084122653 postsHow Do You Do?Whirlpool Forums Addict] iiman writes...
Qantas - Wait time 1/5 (approx 15min each time) x3 -Friendliness 1/5 -Helpfulness 1/5 Overall -5
Qantas has had pretty much a regional monopoly by industry standards in the western world since Ansett went under. They have something like 40% of the Oceania market, where was in USA, southwest, delta, united, and american airlines have around 10-20% each. Lufthansa has ~20% of the European market.
Their strategy because of this is to get people to spend more e.g. take more flights more often, go business class, buy their insurance etc. You can see it in how differently they treat their customers across the loyalty tiers. < Gold vs. Gold vs. Platinum there's massive differences.
I reckon it was only a matter of time before standards dropped. Probably will pick up their game once Virgin gets back on their feet post Covid.
[User #6486197282 postsStBarthWhirlpool Forums Addict] Bob9 writes...
The problem is customer service – not the pilots, planes or schedules.
I have very similar thoughts about Qantas, as I enjoy flying on them although the domestic J product was suffered the death of a thousand cuts over the last decade and a half.
Alan Joyce focusses on the savings from closing the Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane call centres and opening new call centres in Suva, Manila, and expanding the Cape Town call centre.
Sure there are savings, but hugely significant costs to the airline too in the form of reputational damage, and lost business from customers who book with other airlines to avoid running the Qantas gauntlet, including lack of support when things often go wrong.
The baggage savings are another example of this, where they sacked their own Qantas baggage handlers who were great, and outsourced to Swissport. They now have 1 in 10 or 1 in 11 bags delayed or miss flights, and numerous flights cancelled because luggage and cargo were not loaded correctly, had to be unloaded and reloaded, and then having the flight cancelled because the crew timed out while the luggage was being unloaded and reloaded.
Alan Joyce would no doubt say that technology has impacted domestic business bookings and he is right, but I also find it easier to try to do Zoom meetings or videoconference now to avoid running the Qantas gauntlet especially where the product is not as good as it once was, and all the things that might potentially go wrong travelling with Qantas and the lack of customer support provided, where I can.
There are other reasons business travel is down as well, as I have noticed I have come home sick from the last couple of domestic trips so I can safely say I have now have had Covid.
But as far as Qantas and their savings are concerned, there have been savings but also significant reputational damage and costs through lost business as well.
I wonder if they ever look at that the business they have potentially lost and compare it to the savings.
[User #6486197282 postsStBarthWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
The AFR recently published a highly critical article following Alan Joyce's announcement of a $400 million return of capital to shareholders, arguing that Alan Joyce was leaving Qantas with a ticking timebomb due to under investment in the Qantas fleet.
This is a long article that I have edited down, the full article in the link below.
"In 2008, Joyce inherited Geoff Dixon’s order for 20 A380s and 65 787s and a fleet whose average age “is forecast to remain between 8.5 and 8.9 years [based on] the existing contractually committed long-term fleet plan…”
Until June 2019, nearly 11 years into the job, Joyce had never ordered a single new aircraft for Qantas mainline.
Joyce might’ve been right to defer and then cancel eight A380s, though those could’ve been cycled in to replace the oldest ones (now 14 years old). Reducing the 787 order to just 25 inarguably killed a great deal of potential growth. The average age of the fleet, meanwhile, has blown out to 14.7 years while Qantas has returned more than $3 billion to shareholders.
The Qantas fleet has never been this old.
The A330s are now, on average, 16 years old (the eldest are 20), yet Qantas has still ordered no replacement for them. Doing so will require capex – not built into forecasts – of approximately $US9 billion ($13.5 billion) at list prices, and then take many years to arrive.
The mainline domestic fleet of 737-800s is now, on average, 15 years old (nearly a third of them are 20), and is worked harder than almost any other 737 fleet in the world. These 74 planes are at the absolute twilight of their usable lives and replacing them will cost approximately $US8.5 billion at list prices. Qantas placed that order, for A320neos, with Airbus in May this year. Airlines have been receiving this aircraft since 2016 but Qantas will get its first just before Christmas of 2023.
Qantas has also ordered 12 A350-1000ULRs, which can fly non-stop from Australia to London and New York, to arrive from 2025. These will cost $US4.2 billion at list prices....
By rough calculations, in the next decade, the Qantas Group will need to spend up to $US28 billion to replace its fleet without even growing it. Bear in mind this is based on list prices, to which airlines command significant discounts, though this estimate also excludes any replacement of its A380s.
Qantas also needs major, urgent technology investment. qantas.com is absurdly unreliable...."
